description:
EcoSynth: The Earth Information Jukebox

EcoSynth turns NASA Earth science satellite images into real-time music and soundscapes. By converting colors, brightness, and climate changes into audio using web technology, it allows everyone—including blind and low-vision users—to hear how our planet is changing.
summary:
EcoSynth: The Earth Information Jukebox
Bullet How it works: A web app that turns NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) satellite visuals into real-time music. Pixel colors control musical pitch, brightness controls volume, and a timeline slider shifts the tempo across decades of climate data.
Bullet Benefits & Impact: Makes complex Earth science accessible to blind and low-vision users and engaging for students by letting anyone hear how our planet changes.
Bullet Tools Used: NASA EIC datasets, HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas API, Web Audio API (Tone.js), and Canva.
Bullet Creativity & Design: Maps satellite colors to harmonious musical scales so data sounds like expressive music rather than noise, built with screen-reader support and smooth browser performance.
